items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The context is the mortal world among lowest men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be given after proper testing?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is a fit recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter of the text emerging from Candradvīpa concludes at this point?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth
The section is called a chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter of the Candradvīpa text.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The object known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The Kaula determination is known by the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
The locus of dissolution is sought
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks for a full account of where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme and transcendent qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The reality in question is defined by supreme, partless, eternal, and pure qualities.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is equated with the haṃsa, the individual empowered by śakti.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: In what form is the vital air said to be present within all living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath
It is situated in all beings
Its presence is universal among living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is unusual; taken as describing the situated principle.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul declared to be immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated supreme
The subject is called Śiva
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, that principle is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received through traditional transmission?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through successive tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: The teaching is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the claimed efficacy of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone
The knowledge is received by hearing
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge that has been heard...

rows.grounds: object of practice or state attained

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner attains an ochre state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: Six months of practice leads to a renunciant state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to ochre robes or a renunciant condition.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What liberation and companionship result from the prescribed spiritual practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
These are presented as outcomes
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from disease and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What specific teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
It has been told to Bhairavī
The communication is presented as completed
items.inference: The instruction on the soul's practice has been fully conveyed to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What qualities must a recipient possess to be worthy of receiving this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have a resolved mind
items.inference: Only a fully endowed and resolute person is fit to receive the teaching.
uncertainties: Case mismatch between genitive and locative suggests flexible reference to the recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence must not be given
It is identified as the essence of the yoginīs
It is described as their origin or source
items.inference: The sacred Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, is restricted from indiscriminate transmission.
uncertainties: sambhavam may function appositionally despite case difference.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, the origin belonging to the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body from ignorance to purity is being claimed now?
premises: The body is now described as pure
It was previously struck by the veil of ignorance
The change is marked as occurring today
items.inference: The speaker claims a present purification of a body formerly veiled by ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic is the overcoming of time
This overcoming is described as auspicious
items.inference: The speaker seeks instruction on the auspicious conquest of time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or overcoming; context favors overcoming.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed without doubt?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching confidently asserts that death can be destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected while engaging the nectar at its source?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar
The means involves the tip of essence
Even a wise person may be burning
items.inference: Even the wise may experience burning when contacting the nectar's essence.
uncertainties: The exact physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa is unclear.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn when engaging the tip of nectar with the tip of its essence.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the palate is prescribed for practice?
premises: The action is located at the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner should draw in the air
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: The prescribed technique is to slowly draw in breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing attention at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is that it has been practiced
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: One year of this practice destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this has been practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one who has mastered this practice?
premises: Poison does not enter the body
This holds even if bitten
The biting agents are great serpents
items.inference: The practitioner becomes immune to poison even from great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
